BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Sum of an Array
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 3 uses <= instead of <, reading nums[nums.length] (undefined) and turning total into NaN.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Append to User Cart
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 1 uses a mutable default list cart=[], which persists across calls so b contains both items.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Fetch User Profile
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 3 misses await before res.json(), so data is a Promise and data.name is undefined.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Admin Access Check
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 uses assignment (=) instead of equality (==), always setting role to 1 and granting access.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Sort Prices Ascending
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 3 calls .sort() without a comparator, sorting strings so [10, 2, 1] becomes [1, 10, 2].

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Keep Even Numbers
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 4 checks n % 2 == 1 (odd numbers) instead of n % 2 == 0 (even numbers).

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Avoid Mutating Input Object
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 copies the reference instead of cloning ({ ...player }), mutating the caller's object.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Safe Division
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 divides by b before checking if b == 0, crashing with ZeroDivisionError.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Countdown Loop
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 3 increments i++ instead of decrementing i--, causing an infinite loop.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Remove Negative Values
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 4 mutates the list while iterating over it, skipping adjacent negative numbers.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Filter Rows with NULL Email
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 3 uses = NULL instead of IS NULL; in SQL, comparing with = NULL never matches.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Parse Integer Input
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 3 checks val === NaN, which is always false! Use Number.isNaN(val) instead.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: String Buffer Copy
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 allocates only 5 bytes, leaving no room for the null terminator '\0' (buffer overflow).

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Check Key in Dict
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 4 indexes user['default_role'] directly without .get(), raising KeyError if missing.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Return Object From Arrow Function
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 1 opens a function block instead of wrapping the object literal in parentheses: ({ name, active: true }).

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Check Error Before Use
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 uses data before checking err != nil, processing empty/partial output on failure.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Strict Equality on API Status
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 uses assignment code = 201 inside the condition instead of ===.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Reverse String Check
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 3 calls .reverse() on a Python str, which raises AttributeError (use clean[::-1]).

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Count Users Per City
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 3 filters an aggregate inside WHERE instead of HAVING COUNT(*) > 10.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Array Map Return
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 3 is missing the return keyword inside the block body, returning [undefined, ...].

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Integer Floor Average
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 4 uses integer floor division // instead of /, truncating decimals like 2.5 to 2.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Switch Statement Fallthrough
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 misses break;, causing case 1 to fall through and overwrite msg with "WARN".

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Compare Object Equality
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 compares object references with === instead of comparing a.x === b.x, always returning false for distinct objects.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Modify Tuple Element
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 3 tries to assign coords[0] = val on an immutable Python tuple, raising TypeError.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Async Loop Delay
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 1 declares var i (function-scoped), so all 3 timeouts print 3 instead of 0, 1, 2 (use let i).

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Shadow Built-in List
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 overwrites Python's built-in list() with a local variable, causing TypeError on line 5.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Update Single User Email
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 has no WHERE id = 42 clause, overwriting every single user's email in the entire table!

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Check Empty Array
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 checks truthiness of arr — in JS an empty array [] is truthy, so check arr.length > 0.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Integer Division Percentage
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 divides two ints (hits / total) before converting to double, truncating 3/4 to 0!

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Compare String to None
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 compares against the string 'None' instead of `if name is None:`.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Floating-Point Price Check
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 relies on exact float equality; 0.3 - (0.1 + 0.2) is -5.55e-17, not 0 (compare in integer cents).

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Nil Map Assignment
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 writes to a nil map without make(map[string]int), causing a runtime panic.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: JSON Parse Without Try/Catch
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 throws an unhandled SyntaxError if raw is corrupted or empty string instead of wrapping in try/catch.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Modify Set While Iterating
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 4 mutates the set during iteration, raising RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: ForEach With Async/Await
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 uses Array.forEach which ignores returned Promises — saveAll returns before DB writes finish (use for..of or Promise.all).

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Integer Equality vs Identity
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 uses `is` (object identity) instead of `==`; Python only caches small ints (-5..256), failing for larger numbers.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Divide By Zero in Metric
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 divides by impressions without NULLIF(impressions, 0), crashing when a new campaign has 0 impressions.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Missing Break in Switch
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 4 omits break;, so code 1 falls through and returns 'High'.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Shallow Copy Nested List
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 1 repeats references to the SAME inner list 3 times, setting column 0 of EVERY row to 9!

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Dangling Pointer Return
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 3 returns the address of local stack variable x, which is destroyed as soon as makeNum returns.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Regex Global State Trap
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 1 uses the /g flag on a shared RegExp, advancing lastIndex between calls and causing alternating false negatives.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Defer Inside Infinite Loop
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 3 defers Close() until the enclosing function exits, leaking thousands of open file descriptors during the loop.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: String Join on Integers
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 passes ints directly to str.join(), raising TypeError (use map(str, nums)).

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Object Key Coercion
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 4 uses an object as a plain-object key, stringifying both userA and userB to '[object Object]' (use Map).

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: LIKE Wildcard Missing
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 has no % wildcard (e.g. '%Pro%'), so LIKE acts like exact equality = 'Pro'.

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Swapping Variables Accidentally
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 overwrites a before saving its original value, leaving both a and b equal to 20 (use a, b = b, a).

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Array Reverse Mutates Original
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 mutates the caller's array in-place! Use [...list].reverse() or list.toReversed().

BUG_SNIPPETS.title: Off-By-One Array Index
BUG_SNIPPETS.explanation: Line 2 writes to index 4 on a 4-element array (valid indices are 0..3), causing undefined behavior.

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: Flash Sale DB Meltdown
OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.situation: Primary PostgreSQL CPU just spiked to 100% during a flash sale. Checkout latency jumped from 120ms to 9.4s.

choices.text: Enable read-replica routing & cache hot product queries in Redis
choices.outcome: Read traffic drops 75% immediately and checkout stabilizes!

choices.text: Restart the database server right away with zero drain
choices.outcome: Cold cache + dropped connections cause a retry storm and 4 minutes of downtime.

choices.text: Run ALTER TABLE to rebuild all indexes live during peak traffic
choices.outcome: Table locks freeze every active checkout query.

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: Memory Leak After v2.14 Deploy
OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.situation: Ten minutes after deploying v2.14, API containers are OOM-killing every 3 minutes.

choices.text: Roll back immediately to v2.13, then capture a heap dump in staging
choices.outcome: Rollback restores stability in 45 seconds while preserving evidence to debug safely.

choices.text: Triple RAM limits and keep v2.14 running until tomorrow
choices.outcome: The leak still fills the larger containers 20 minutes later.

choices.text: SSH into production containers and live-edit code
choices.outcome: Auto-scaler replaces the containers anyway, wiping your hotfix.

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: CDN Cache Stampede
OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.situation: A homepage JSON endpoint cache expired simultaneously across 50,000 mobile users, hammering your origin.

choices.text: Turn on stale-while-revalidate + request coalescing at the edge
choices.outcome: Edge collapses 50k concurrent requests into 1 origin fetch.

choices.text: Disable caching completely so users get fresh data
choices.outcome: Origin servers melt under 100% uncached traffic.

choices.text: Return HTTP 200 with an empty array {} for everyone
choices.outcome: Latency looks green, but every user sees a blank broken app!

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: Expired TLS Certificate
OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.situation: Alerts fire: browsers are showing "Your connection is not private" on your main API domain.

choices.text: Renew & deploy the cert via ACME/managed edge and verify the full chain
choices.outcome: HTTPS handshakes recover globally within minutes.

choices.text: Redirect all API traffic from HTTPS down to plain HTTP
choices.outcome: HSTS blocks downgrade and exposes auth tokens in plaintext!

choices.text: Tell users to clear cookies and wait 24 hours
choices.outcome: Expired certificates don't fix themselves — outage drags on.

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: Payment Gateway Hanging
OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.situation: Your external payment API started taking 25 seconds to time out, exhausting all backend worker threads.

choices.text: Add strict 3s timeouts + a circuit breaker with graceful retry queue
choices.outcome: Rest of the site stays fast and checkout degrades cleanly.

choices.text: Increase HTTP client timeout from 25s to 120s
choices.outcome: Threads pile up 5x faster, taking down login and browsing too.

choices.text: Auto-retry failed requests 10 times in a tight loop
choices.outcome: Retry storm DDoSes both your workers and the payment provider.

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: Disk 100% Full on Log Server
OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.situation: API writes are failing with ENOSPC because verbose debug logs filled the 500GB root disk overnight.

choices.text: Truncate rotated old logs safely, drop log level to INFO, and enable logrotate
choices.outcome: Disk space frees immediately without breaking open file handles.

choices.text: Run rm -rf /var/log/* while services still hold open file descriptors
choices.outcome: Deleted files stay allocated until processes restart, keeping disk at 100%!

choices.text: Reboot the server without freeing space first
choices.outcome: Services fail to boot cleanly because the OS cannot write PID files.

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: Accidental API Key Commit
OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.situation: A developer accidentally pushed a live cloud admin key to a public GitHub repo 4 minutes ago.

choices.text: Revoke & rotate the key immediately, audit access logs, then scrub git history
choices.outcome: Key becomes useless within seconds before automated scrapers abuse it.

choices.text: Just push a second commit deleting the key from the file
choices.outcome: The key remains readable forever in git history and bots already scraped it!

choices.text: Make the repo private tomorrow morning during standup
choices.outcome: Automated bots scan public GitHub pushes in under 30 seconds.

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: N+1 Query Explosion
OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.situation: Adding 'mutual friends count' to the feed made page load fire 301 SQL queries per request.

choices.text: Batch fetch counts with a single JOIN / IN (...) query and add an index
choices.outcome: 301 queries drop to 2 queries; P99 latency plummets!

choices.text: Spin up 50 more API pods without touching the query
choices.outcome: More pods just hammer the single database 50x harder.

choices.text: Wrap every query in a 500ms sleep to slow down traffic
choices.outcome: Requests now take 2.5 minutes each and time out.

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: CORS Broken in Production
OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.situation: Frontend on app.example.com can't call api.example.com after a gateway config change.

choices.text: Allow exact origin https://app.example.com and handle OPTIONS preflight cleanly
choices.outcome: Browser preflight passes securely without opening wildcard access.

choices.text: Set Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * alongside Allow-Credentials: true
choices.outcome: Browsers explicitly reject wildcard '*' when credentials are enabled!

choices.text: Tell users to launch Chrome with --disable-web-security
choices.outcome: Totally unusable for real users and a huge security hazard.

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: Runaway Cron Job Overlap
OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.situation: An hourly billing job now takes 75 minutes, so multiple copies overlap and double-charge customers.

choices.text: Add a distributed lock + idempotency keys on billing transactions
choices.outcome: Overlapping runs exit cleanly and duplicate charges become impossible.

choices.text: Change the cron schedule to run every 15 minutes instead
choices.outcome: Now 5 copies pile up simultaneously!

choices.text: Ignore it and refund angry customers manually next week
choices.outcome: Support queue explodes and payment processor flags your account.

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: DNS TTL Misconfiguration
OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.situation: You're migrating traffic to a new load balancer IP, but DNS TTL is set to 86400 seconds (24 hours).

choices.text: Lower TTL to 60s at least 24h before cutover, then switch and verify
choices.outcome: Clean zero-downtime migration with rapid rollback capability.

choices.text: Shut down the old load balancer immediately after changing DNS
choices.outcome: Users with cached DNS records hit a dead IP for up to 24 hours.

choices.text: Ask ISPs worldwide to flush their recursive resolvers manually
choices.outcome: Not possible across the public internet.

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: Database Connection Pool Exhausted
OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.situation: Serverless functions scaled to 1,000 instances and hit PostgreSQL's max_connections limit (200).

choices.text: Place a connection pooler (PgBouncer / Hyperdrive) in transaction mode in front of DB
choices.outcome: Thousands of short serverless bursts multiplex smoothly over 50 DB connections.

choices.text: Raise max_connections to 50,000 on a 4GB RAM database
choices.outcome: Each connection consumes RAM, instantly OOM-crashing PostgreSQL.

choices.text: Disable connection closing so sockets stay open forever
choices.outcome: Idle connections permanently starve new requests.

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: Deadlock on Inventory Table
OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.situation: Concurrent orders updating two SKUs in opposite order trigger frequent SQL deadlocks.

choices.text: Lock/update SKU rows in a deterministic sorted ID order + retry transient deadlocks
choices.outcome: Consistent lock ordering eliminates circular waits completely.

choices.text: Remove all database transactions and allow negative inventory
choices.outcome: You oversell limited stock by 400 units.

choices.text: Lock the entire database exclusively for every user click
choices.outcome: Throughput collapses to 1 checkout at a time.

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: Missing Pagination on /api/orders

choices.outcome: Payload shrinks from 180MB to 12KB and responds in 18ms.

choices.text: Return all 180,000 rows as gzipped JSON and hope mobile Safari survives
choices.outcome: Server still buffers 180k rows in memory and mobile browsers freeze.

choices.text: Delete orders older than 30 days from production

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: JWT Secret Rotated Without Grace Window

choices.outcome: Anyone can forge an admin token in 5 seconds!

choices.text: Force every user to reset their password via email

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: Regex Denial of Service (ReDoS)
OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.situation: A single malformed email input froze a Node.js event loop at 100% CPU for 45 seconds due to catastrophic backtracking.

choices.outcome: CPU drops back to 4% immediately and malicious inputs resolve in microseconds.

choices.text: Double Node.js heap memory to 32GB

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: Split-Brain Redis Failover
OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.situation: A brief network partition left two Redis nodes both thinking they are the primary master, causing conflicting writes.

choices.outcome: Minority partition refuses writes automatically, eliminating split-brain divergence.

choices.text: Run only 2 Redis nodes with quorum set to 1
choices.outcome: Guarantees split-brain on every network hiccup!

choices.text: Flush all Redis keys every 5 minutes via cron
choices.outcome: Destroys active user sessions and causes constant DB stampedes.

choices.text: Run migrations once as a pre-deploy CI/CD release step (or init job) using advisory locks
choices.outcome: Exactly one migration runs cleanly before new app pods receive traffic.

choices.text: Add a random 1–3 second sleep before migrating on every pod
choices.outcome: Pods still collide whenever migrations take longer than 3 seconds.

choices.text: Manually edit production tables in pgAdmin while traffic is live
choices.outcome: Unrepeatable drift breaks staging and future deployments.

choices.text: Redesign partition key with high cardinality (e.g. `userId` or salted shard suffix)

choices.text: Keep `country` as key and add more secondary indexes
choices.outcome: Secondary indexes amplify write load on the exact same hot partition!

choices.text: Drop 80% of Indian user requests silently
choices.outcome: Catastrophic outage for your largest user base.

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: Unbounded Webhook Retries Storm

choices.text: Switch to exponential backoff with random jitter and cap max attempts
choices.outcome: Spreads retries gracefully and prevents thundering herds when the partner recovers.

choices.text: Retry every 1 second forever so it succeeds faster
choices.outcome: Saturates all outbound sockets and gets your IP banned.

choices.text: Delete the webhook feature from production

OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.title: Stale Browser Cache After Deploy
OUTAGE_SCENARIOS.situation: Users see broken JS errors after a deploy because `app.js` was cached for 1 year without a content hash in its filename.

choices.text: Use content-hashed asset filenames (`app.9f3a2c.js`) with `no-cache` on `index.html`
choices.outcome: Users get instant fresh bundles on every deploy while keeping long-lived CDN caching.
